extracted.subtask_description: Practical, prescriptive guidance for mothers and step-mothers on managing relationships with children, training them in household tasks, protecting them from adult burdens, and dealing with the challenges of youth. Emphasises temperament, tact, age-appropriate duties, and moral training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make yourself love the little ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Make yourself love the little ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you already love them, 'half the battle is won.' The author urges step-mothers to begin with their own feelings and to cultivate genuine affection rather than rely on duty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control your own nerves and composure when managing children
rubrics_metrics.description: In driving a restless horse, it is absolutely essential that you should not be at all nervous yourself; the same principle applies to children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a firm, steady, yet gentle control. If you cannot control yourself the children know it, and attempts to govern them by nervousness or vehemence aggravate the evil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin and govern children with love
rubrics_metrics.description: Their government must have love at its beginning, continuing and ending if it would be successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Love is presented as the foundation of any effective discipline or training; without it, other measures fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add patience, tact, and pity to maternal love
rubrics_metrics.description: You are laboring under a disadvantage in that the hyphenized 'step' must precede your name of mother; you have need to add to your love patience, and to that tact, and to that pity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let children see exasperation; guard the harsh tongue; practice patience and pity so as to win their affection over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard the harsh tongue; avoid scolding and unjust reproach
rubrics_metrics.description: If the children exasperate you, do not let them guess it. Keep a rigid guard upon the harsh tongue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid quick exclamations like 'Stop that noise!' or 'Do be quiet!' The step-mother gains trust when children cannot point to a single unjust act committed against them; unjust punishments are remembered for years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unjust punishments; children remember injustice
rubrics_metrics.description: Boys and girls remember an injustice for many years; they often do not forget the undeserved blow, the unprovoked sarcasm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful in correction—children forgive fair chastisement more readily than undeserved blame; unjust accusations create long-lasting resentment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate tact by imagining the child's perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps the best rule by which to learn it is the old one of 'Put yourself in his place.' Reverse the positions and imagine yourself a hot-headed, sore-hearted, prejudiced child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly practice seeing corrections and interactions from the child's viewpoint; this habit will make tactful patience second nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not correct children publicly or complain to their father
rubrics_metrics.description: If you can possibly avoid it, do not correct the children in the presence of other people, or complain to their father of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telling the father 'Your mother tells me that you have done so-and-so' lays foundations of distrust. Prefer to let them domineer over you rather than to prejudice the father against them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak often and reverently of the children's deceased mother
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk to them often and reverently of their own mother. Do not allow them to forget her, and guard against the entrance of any jealous feeling into this sacred duty of keeping her memory fresh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the children's mother as a sacred trust; reassure children that their mother's memory and place in the 'eternal home' will remain—this helps win their love and confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train children in age-appropriate housework
rubrics_metrics.description: Children ought to be trained to do housework and to make themselves useful in ways in which the young hands and feet can save the older ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start early but do not overwork or make a drudge of the child; tasks should not interfere with outdoor exercise and play; training prepares them for adult responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin usefulness as soon as the child can walk
rubrics_metrics.description: By the time your child can walk, he may begin to make himself useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: toddlers can be given a 'baby duster,' bring boots and gloves, ask to 'help mamma'—even if the help is imperfect, it is preferable to idle fretting and fosters a helpful habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oblige children to tidy up their toys and belongings
rubrics_metrics.description: When your small daughter has finished with her toys, she should be obliged to put them away in a box kept for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This spares the mother bending and stooping and teaches the child responsibility and the satisfaction of 'grown-up' duties (dolly to bed, furniture in place).

rubrics_metrics.name: Let children assist with bed-making and simple kitchen tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: When making the beds, allow the little girl to hand you the pillows; when making pies, place a small portion of dough for the child to knead and set in the oven as her contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involving children in small tasks keeps them occupied, teaches processes, and fosters pride in being useful even if their work is imperfect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress domestic competence with age (girls by ten)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the time your girl is ten years old, she should be equal to making her own bed, dusting and keeping her own little room in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach gradually, 'line upon line.' Have an adult help with heavy lifting; train her to notice small details that make a thrifty housekeeper rather than a slattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate an 'eye for dirt' and attention to small housekeeping details
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate your daughter's eye for dust, dirt and cobwebs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out 'hall-marks' of housewifery repeatedly; small details (soap-cup, finger-smears, fluff in corners) matter in forming a neat housekeeper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign regular domestic tasks and teach money value by paying for work
rubrics_metrics.description: As she grows older, let her straighten parlors every morning, make the cake on Saturdays, and when she can entirely relieve you of mending and laundry, pay her a stated amount each week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This develops independence, pride, earning of pocket-money, and early lessons in the value of dollars and cents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervise children's early work with patience; do not judge too harshly
rubrics_metrics.description: Few children are born with a sensitive conscience regarding their work, so the mother will, at first, find it necessary to keep an eye on all the tasks performed by the willing, if often careless, girl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember your own youth; be gentle and forbearing while correcting and training; patience will yield a child who models 'as mamma does.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach boys domestic rudiments without fear of making them effeminate
rubrics_metrics.description: While especially expedient that girls receive domestic training, the boys of the family should not be exempt from their share of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching darning, mending, and basic cookery makes boys more considerate of women and more capable; some boys show aptitude for dainty work that benefits them lifelong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach boys to keep their rooms and possessions in order
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach your son that it is his business to keep his own room in order, and that there is no more reason why his sister should follow him up replacing what he has disarranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inculcate neat habits; make the boy aware of the disorder he causes and the consideration required to tidy it—lessons in sympathy and responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not thrust adult anxieties or responsibilities upon children
rubrics_metrics.description: I want to enter my protest against thrusting upon children the care-taking thought that should not be theirs for years to come.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children who hear constant adult complaints may become inured, hard-hearted, or miserable; adult worries (financial fears, business troubles) should not be discussed in a way that terrifies or saddens young children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach prudence and economy without making children carry adult burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach your children to be careful, teach them prudence and economy, but let them be taught as children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance teaching responsible habits with preserving a child's innocence; do not convert baby troubles into adult anxieties for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exploiting a child's sensibilities; do not overuse appeals to pity
rubrics_metrics.description: The forcing of a child's sympathies sometimes produces a hardening effect; repeatedly drawing upon a child's sensibilities can make him callous or silly in response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not repeatedly dramatize dire possibilities (e.g., 'Suppose poor mamma should die') to elicit sympathy; these appeals often produce inadequate or comic responses and can be emotionally harmful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not discuss business failures or financial distress with young children
rubrics_metrics.description: An otherwise judicious father talks over all his business difficulties with his seven-year-old son—the boy's white, set face would have alarmed a more observant man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents should shield young children from details of bills, failures, and financial uncertainty; such talk can cause lasting fear (e.g., fear of 'poorhouse').

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that youth's 'freshness' is natural and requires patience
rubrics_metrics.description: Youth is not a sin to be condemned; 'freshness' (self-conceit, pretence of doubt, sentimental musings) is almost inseparable from this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older people should remember their own youth and treat young persons with patience and forbearance rather than harsh condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-praising or snubbing clever young people; give intelligent appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: If your girl is clever, do not tell her so, or repeat to others in her presence her bright observations. But on the other hand, do not snub her or allow her to feel that her intellect is inferior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stimulate a child with love and appreciation that is intelligent rather than blind admiration; indiscriminate praise or undue public elevation can produce conceit or ridicule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prune and train youth: encourage some traits, repress others
rubrics_metrics.description: Young people need training, encouragement and urging in some directions, repression and pruning in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the gardener analogy: do not let youthful tendencies run unchecked nor do you 'cut off all the stalks within an inch of the roots'—exercise balanced guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model tolerance and charitable speech as parents
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us older people set an example of tolerance and charitable speech; too often our children are but reproductions of ourselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating tact, unselfishness, and tender charity teaches children by example to avoid wholesale intolerance and uncharitableness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage habits of kindly speech; restrain unkind criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming a pledge or society to repress unkind criticism can help young people cultivate the habit of speaking kindly or saying nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice and small pledges can slowly grow into a sincere habit of charity in speech; the author gives example of ten girls forming such a society.
